By default, Ancile changes Windows Update to "check/notify". This means that Windows will check for new updates and notify the user if new updates are available, but will not download or install any new updates. After it makes that change it uninstalls and then hides the updates listed in "data\updates\uninstall\ancile_updateuninst.lst" (This is a text file that can be viewed in notepad).

Once Ancile has finished, updates that have been uninstalled and hidden will remain uninstalled and hidden (as long as MS doesn't re-issue them), and any future updates to Windows will require that the user manually run Windows Update.

If you want to not set Windows Update to "check/notify" you can set "MODWINUPDATE" to "N" in "config.ini". This will disable the change to Windows Update and still uninstall and hide the individual updates. For systems that have already been changed to "check/notify" you will need to manually change that back.

I've heard that Microsoft has re-issued some updates in the past. All this means is that they have used some method to push the update back into the user's Windows Update queue. What do you mean with uninstall and hide? Isn't it already gone by being uninstalled? What should we hide them from if they are no longer there?

Windows Update works by looking through a list of available updates for your system and installing what it thinks are needed (That's over simplified, but close enough). If you uninstall an update, the next time WU runs it will see that you are missing the uninstalled update and install it again. To prevent this we tell WU to hide the update. Once it's been hidden WU will never install the hidden update.
